why: Re-measures the ten-second first-terminal gate on a release binary that actually contains the recent startup, wake-recovery and terminal-pane changes. The previously cited release binary predates them and no longer exists on disk.

local.warmupNote: A first run straight after a fresh link and cold OS caches measured 9158ms on an earlier link of this same source tree. That warmup figure is not representative of a normal launch; the repeated runs below are.

remote.fixture: ephemeral isolated HOME + localhost OpenSSH sshd, key authentication

localPtySurvivesSuspendedCpu.why: Local sessions are deliberately excluded from host-wake recovery, which is only correct if a local shell keeps working after the CPU is suspended and resumed.
localPtySurvivesSuspendedCpu.method: Spawn /bin/zsh -i over a pipe, SIGSTOP the process for 2.5s, SIGCONT, then run the same arithmetic marker command again.
localPtySurvivesSuspendedCpu.limitation: SIGSTOP/SIGCONT reproduces the suspended-CPU half of sleep but not the real power-management transition, lid close, or network renegotiation. A real lid-close observation on hardware is still outstanding.

limitations: The remote round-trip uses a preseeded localhost key-authenticated workspace; it does not prove first-user host selection, password/agent/jump authentication, or WAN latency.
The shell prompt is rendered on the xterm canvas and stays diagnostic-only through AX; local PTY and shell-interaction probes prove interactivity separately.
Host sleep/wake recovery is covered by frontend regression tests only; the real lid-close path is not exercised here.
The bundle is unsigned and unnotarized, so Gatekeeper launch behaviour on a clean machine is not covered.
Human physical keyboard, real macOS IME, Option/dead key, Windows OpenSSH Agent/Pageant/ConPTY, and serial hardware acceptance remain unverified.

supersedes.reason: That file measured release binary 7a7fc91e…, which the runners relink away on every build and which predates the startup, wake-recovery and terminal-pane changes.
